details: This package is a modified WhatsApp (Baileys) client library that covertly enrols the connecting account into an unknown WhatsApp channel and forges that channel's attribution onto outgoing messages. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js a top-level setTimeout fires 90 seconds after the module is loaded and sends a w:mex FOLLOW query for the channel identifier 120363407277177688@newsletter (stored base64-encoded as MTIwMzYzNDA3Mjc3MTc3Njg4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=); every error is swallowed, so the subscription happens silently and is not described anywhere in the package. In lib/Socket/rahmad.js (class kikyy, required from lib/Socket/messages-send.js) every generated message is given forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo {newsletterJid: 120363407277177688@newsletter, newsletterName: "shenvn."} plus fabricated forwardingScore 99999, isForwarded, disappearingMode and businessMessageForwardInfo fields, so traffic sent by the application appears forwarded from and attributed to that channel. The preinstall hook engine-requirements.js only checks the Node.js major version (>=20). No credentials, tokens, environment variables,.npmrc, SSH or cloud key files are read, and the only network destinations in the code are the WhatsApp service (wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat, v[.]whatsapp[.]net) and the npm registry; the injected behaviour uses WhatsApp's own protocol rather than a separate controller host.
